title: Isolation of novel sequences targeting highly variable viral protein hemagglutinin☆
author: Xu, Wu, et al.
materials: The digested SK(−) vector and the HA assembly products were ligated with at an approximate molar ratio of 1:7 in the refrigerator (5 °C). The ligation mixtures were precipitated with ethanol and dissolved in 10 μl of sterile double distilled H2O or less, and electroporated to E. coli ElectroMax-DH10B strain (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA) [5]. Cells were plated onto LB/ampicillin plates. PCR was performed with primers 4 and 9 after microwave treatment of toothpick touched colonies [6], and 1550 bp PCR amplicons were visualized on agarose gel (Fig. 3). The positive rate was 54.5%, which was about 26-fold higher than that of the previous FMDV gene fragment libraries before the enrichment procedure [1]. The clones of E. coli DNA library carrying hemagglutinin gene fragment failed to grow, most likely resulted from stressful peptides expressed from the partial gene. Therefore the engineering of a full-length gene was advantageous, especially for genes from highly virulent viruses. Two of the putative positive clones were successfully sequenced and found to be novel. Bacteria were washed from the plates, and pooled, and treated as aforementioned. PCR amplicons were subsequently sequenced and shown to harbor multiple sequences (Fig. 4). The presence of virtually all the designed bases in the degenerated sites suggests that the library carried many clones.

steps.title: Design semi‑random oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Design three semi‑random oligos (oligo 1, oligo 2, oligo 3) based on the HA sequence alignment (see Table 1, Fig. 1).

steps.title: Initial assembly of oligo2 and oligo3
steps.instruction: Set up a 20 µL PCR reaction containing 2 µL oligo 2, 2 µL oligo 3, PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase (as supplied), and 2.5 % (v/v) 2‑pyrrolidone. Run: 94 °C 2 min; 4 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 33 °C 60 s, 72 °C 20 s; final extension 72 °C 3 min; hold 4 °C 1 h.

steps.title: Add oligo1 and oligo3 to complete subassembly
steps.instruction: To the previous mixture add 3 µL oligo 1, 2 µL oligo 3 and 0.5 µL PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase. Thermocycle: 94 °C 2 min; 15 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 33 °C 60 s, 72 °C 20 s; final extension 72 °C 3 min. This yields a 127‑bp subassembly product.

steps.title: Amplify leftmost 355‑bp fragment
steps.instruction: Perform PCR with HA gene template, primers 4 and 5, PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase and 2.5 % 2‑pyrrolidone in a suitable volume. Cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 30 °C 60 s, 72 °C 80 s; final extension 72 °C 3 min. Product size: 355 bp.

steps.title: Overlap PCR to generate 468‑bp product
steps.instruction: Combine the 127‑bp and 355‑bp products as templates, add primers 4 and 10, PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase and 2.5 % 2‑pyrrolidone. Cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 30 °C 60 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min. Product size: 468 bp.

steps.title: Amplify 560‑bp and 574‑bp fragments
steps.instruction: Set up two separate PCRs using HA gene template, PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase, 2.5 % 2‑pyrrolidone and either primer pair 6/7 or 8/9. Cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 30 °C 60 s, 72 °C 80 s; final extension 72 °C 3 min. Products: 560 bp (6/7) and 574 bp (8/9).

steps.title: Overlap PCR to create 1130‑bp product with RETRGLP
steps.instruction: Mix the 560‑bp and 574‑bp products, add primers 6 and 9, PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase and 2.5 % 2‑pyrrolidone. Cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 35 cycles of 94 °C 20 s, 26 °C 60 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min. Product size: 1130 bp containing the RETRGLP insertion at the HA cleavage site.

steps.title: Final overlapping PCR for full‑length HA
steps.instruction: Combine the 468‑bp and 1130‑bp products, add primers 4, 9 and 10, PrimeSTAR DNA polymerase and 2.5 % 2‑pyrrolidone. Cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 30 °C 60 s, 72 °C 2 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min. Product size: 1550 bp full‑length HA.

steps.title: Triple‑digest pBluescript SK(−) vector
steps.instruction: Digest 0.98 µg SK(−) vector with 12 U each of BamHI, EcoRI and HindIII in the appropriate buffer for 4 h at 37 °C. Heat‑inactivate enzymes at 75 °C for 15 min. Precipitate DNA with ethanol and dissolve the pellet in 20 µL double‑distilled water.

steps.title: Digest HA assembly products and resuspend
steps.instruction: Treat the HA assembly products identically (triple‑digest with BamHI, EcoRI, HindIII, ethanol precipitation) and resuspend the resulting DNA in 40 µL double‑distilled water.

steps.title: Ligate vector and HA inserts
steps.instruction: Ligate the digested vector and HA inserts at an approximate molar ratio of 1 : 7 in a refrigerated (5 °C) environment. After ligation, precipitate the mixture with ethanol and dissolve the pellet in ≤10 µL sterile double‑distilled water.

steps.title: Electroporate ligation mix into E. coli DH10B
steps.instruction: Electroporate the ligation product into ElectroMax‑DH10B E. coli (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA) using the manufacturer’s ultra‑efficient electroporation protocol.

steps.title: Plate transformed cells on selective medium
steps.instruction: Recover cells and plate on LB agar containing ampicillin. Incubate until colonies appear.

steps.title: Colony PCR after microwave treatment
steps.instruction: Touch individual colonies with a toothpick, apply brief microwave treatment as described, then perform PCR using primers 4 and 9. Visualize the 1550‑bp amplicon on an agarose gel.

steps.title: Sequence positive clones
steps.instruction: Select colonies that yield the correct 1550‑bp band, purify their plasmid DNA and submit for Sanger sequencing. Two clones were confirmed as novel HA sequences.

steps.title: Pool bacterial cultures and re‑sequence amplicons
steps.instruction: Wash bacteria from plates, pool the cultures, repeat the PCR and sequencing steps as above to confirm the presence of multiple designed bases in the degenerated sites.
